prompt: There are those who consider work to be the paramount aspect of life, suggesting that without career success, life loses its meaning. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many people believe that professional achievement is the most important aspect of life and that, without it, existence loses its meaning. I strongly disagree, although I accept that a successful career brings real benefits.

On the one hand, career success can give life direction. Ambitious individuals often regard their work as a way to challenge themselves, and this mindset can produce remarkable results. For example, Aliko Dangote became one of Africa's most successful businessmen through relentless determination, and millions of young people now see him as a role model.

However, a career alone cannot make a life meaningful. Someone may have an impressive job but neglect their character, which can damage their relationships and reputation. Many people judge others by their values and behaviour rather than by their job title. A manager who treats colleagues badly, for instance, is unlikely to be respected, however high his position.

Furthermore, there are many other ways to achieve success within a community. Through hard work, charity and good conduct, ordinary people can influence society more deeply than some professionals. A teacher who mentors poor students, or a volunteer who feeds the homeless, may leave a stronger legacy than a wealthy executive.

In conclusion, I disagree that career success is the paramount element of life, since personality, actions and reputation are often more admired. Nevertheless, work remains important and should not be neglected.
